findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the public instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts.

Ingress on port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with plaintext HTTP only, and egress allows all protocols/ports to any destination, permitting unrestricted data exfiltration or C2 callbacks from a compromised host.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in the EC2 user_data script. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (including via SSRF) and is stored in plaintext in the Terraform state.
The instance does not configure root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and instance credentials/user-data can be stolen through a simple SSRF against 169.254.169.254.
The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch and a default route to an internet gateway, giving it a public IP and direct internet reachability with an open SSH port.
The EBS volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data on the volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also unencrypted at rest and could be exposed if shared or copied.
The VPC flow-log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy is defined for the flow-log bucket, so nothing prevents a public ACL or policy from later exposing network flow records.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true is set, so flow-log evidence in the bucket can be silently overwritten or destroyed, undermining audit integrity.
The bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server access logging configured, so unauthorized access to the security telemetry would go unrecorded.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically exposing workloads to the internet.

The route table shared by both subnets sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway, making every subnet public with no private tier for backend resources.
